svg.title: The ARK Vault wiring, with every part drawn as it looks and all of its terminals. The battery, seen from above, has two bolts: plus near one end and minus near the other, each also taking the wall charger's lead. Run 1, 16 AWG red: battery plus to the inline blade fuse holder (7.5 amp fuse). Run 2, 16 AWG red: the fuse holder to the rocker switch's input pin, seen from behind; the input pin's one spade also takes run 11 (the meter's thin yellow wire, 22 AWG) and run 13 (from the microswitch's NO tab, 22 AWG). Run 3, 16 AWG red: the switch's output pin to a splice; from it run 4 goes to the converter's Input plus and run 5 to the printer's power plug, plus. Run 6, 16 AWG black: battery minus to the meter's thick black wire; the meter's thin black wire (run 10) joins it there. The meter's thick red wire (run 7) goes to a splice; from it run 8 to the converter's Input minus and run 9 to the printer's power plug, minus. The meter's thin red wire (run 12) goes to the microswitch's C tab; its NC tab is not used. The converter's four screw terminals, left to right as printed: Input plus, Input minus, Output minus, Output plus. Runs 14 and 15, 18 AWG red and black: Output plus to the Pi's pin 2 and Output minus to pin 14. The printer's other sockets: USB (its USB lead, run 17, to a black USB port on the Pi), TTL serial and 485, not used. The Raspberry Pi 4 from above: the 40-pin row along one long edge, pin 1 at the end away from the USB ports; Ethernet, two blue USB 3 ports (lower: the library drive; upper: the mesh radio's USB-C cable, run 18) and two black USB 2 ports (one for the printer, one free) along the short edge; USB-C power, two micro HDMI and the audio socket not used; the microSD card underneath. The cooler's fan, run 16, on pins 4 (red), 6 (black) and 8 (blue). The 40 pins enlarged, with every pin's name. Later, for the sun: the solar controller's battery terminals to the battery in 12 AWG through a 20 amp fuse, its panel terminals to the panel, its load terminals not used.

Seen from above, as in the drawing: the top row (even pins) runs along the board’s edge, and pin 1 is the end farthest from the USB ports. Fit the wires with the power off.
← the fan: red on 4 (5 V), black on 6 (ground), blue on 8 (GPIO 14)
Coloured border: a wire goes on it in the Vault.
Later, for the sun (stored in the can, not wired)
a wire hopping over another is not joined to it
Check the converter’s output with a multimeter before
plugging it onto the Pi: 5.0 to 5.25 V, + and − right.
Meter: some put the thick wires the other way round;
check its own sheet. Microswitch: C, NO and NC are
printed on its side. Power switch: a lit one has a
third pin (the light’s −): a thin wire to battery −,
or leave it off and it just won’t light.
The ARK Vault wiring: every part and its terminals
Each number in a circle is a run in the guide’s table, with its wire size.
